title: Fetal Heart Rate Monitoring (NICHD)
sources: Critical Vector — OB Pocket Guide: EFM / Fetal Heart Rate (NICHD 2023)
NICHD / ACOG three-tier fetal heart rate interpretation system

changelog.change: Initial entry — the NICHD three-category system, deceleration types and their mechanism, and the intrauterine-resuscitation steps.

summary: Category I = normal, no action. Category III = abnormal (sinusoidal, OR absent variability with recurrent late/variable decelerations or bradycardia) → intrauterine resuscitation while expediting delivery. Category II (everything in between) → evaluate and take corrective measures, reassess.

rows: I — Normal
ALL of: baseline 110–160, moderate variability (6–25 bpm), NO late or variable decelerations. Early decelerations and accelerations may be present or absent
No action; routine monitoring
II — Indeterminate

Any tracing not I or III — e.g. tachycardia, bradycardia with retained variability, minimal variability, absent variability without recurrent decelerations, recurrent variables with minimal/moderate variability, a prolonged deceleration 2–10 min
Evaluate and take corrective measures (intrauterine resuscitation); reassess. Persistent / worsening Category II near delivery is a reason to expedite
III — Abnormal
Sinusoidal pattern, OR absent baseline variability WITH any of: recurrent late decelerations, recurrent variable decelerations, or bradycardia
Expedite delivery; intrauterine resuscitation while preparing. Associated with abnormal fetal acid-base status
Early
Gradual onset; nadir coincides with the contraction peak; mirrors the contraction
Fetal head compression — BENIGN
Late
Gradual onset; nadir AFTER the contraction peak; returns to baseline after the contraction ends
Uteroplacental insufficiency — significant; recurrent late decels drive management
Variable
ABRUPT onset and offset (< 30 s to nadir); ≥ 15 bpm drop for ≥ 15 s; variable shape and timing
Umbilical cord compression — significance depends on depth, duration, and the retained variability
Prolonged
≥ 15 bpm below baseline for ≥ 2 min but < 10 min
Any cause of acute hypoxia — cord prolapse, abruption, uterine tachysystole, maternal hypotension, rapid descent

items: 1. Reposition — left or right lateral decubitus; knee-chest if cord prolapse.
2. O2 10 L/min via non-rebreather (evidence is weak; brief use is reasonable).
3. IV fluid bolus 500 mL LR — especially for maternal hypotension or tachysystole.
4. STOP oxytocin and/or remove prostaglandin (dinoprostone) immediately.
5. Treat maternal hypotension — ephedrine 5–10 mg IV or phenylephrine 50–100 mcg IV; a tocolytic (terbutaline 0.25 mg SC) for tachysystole.
6. Fetal scalp stimulation — an acceleration of ≥ 15 bpm for ≥ 15 s predicts a scalp pH ≥ 7.20 (a reassuring response).
7. Amnioinfusion for recurrent variable decelerations from cord compression.
If the tracing does not recover promptly → move to delivery.

buildNote: Tier 3. Fetal scalp blood sampling and the STAN (ST-analysis) adjunct are further detail. Category II management algorithms (e.g. the Clark algorithm) could be an expansion.
